What is the area of the quadrilateral EMFP, if the sum of the areas of the triangles $A E D$ and BFC is $\frac{1}{3}$?

Let P=(t,1) on DC. Line AP has points λ(t,1), and diagonal BD satisfies x+y=1, so E=(t/(1+t), 1/(1+t)). Line BP can be parametrized as (1+s(t-1), s), and diagonal AC satisfies x=y, so s=1/(2-t), giving F=(1/(2-t), 1/(2-t)). The area of triangle AED is t/[2(1+t)]. The area of triangle BFC is (1-t)/[2(2-t)]. Given their sum is 1/3, we have t/[2(1+t)] + (1-t)/[2(2-t)] = 1/3. Multiplying out gives (2t-1)^2=0, hence t=1/2. Therefore E=(1/3,2/3), F=(2/3,2/3), M=(1/2,1/2), and P=(1/2,1). Using the shoelace formula for quadrilateral E-M-F-P gives area = 1/12.

Because DP is parallel to AB, use similarity/intercept ratios to locate E on diagonal BD: ED/BD=u/(1+u), so area(AED)=[u/(1+u)]·area(ABD)=u/[2(1+u)]. Then E and F lie one third of the way down from DC to the diagonal midpoint level: E and F are on the line parallel to the bases at height fraction 2/3, with EF equal to one third of the base length. M is halfway between the bases. Therefore EMFP is the union of triangles EFP and EMF with common base EF. Relative to the parallelogram area 1, area(EFP)=1/2·(1/3)·(1/3)=1/18 and area(EMF)=1/2·(1/3)·(1/6)=1/36, so area(EMFP)=1/18+1/36=1/12.
